---
title: "JQI_FinancialSatisfaction_ConfidenceGovernment"
output: html_document
---

```{r Step 1, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# JQI: Financial Satisfaction and Confidence in Government
# ============================================================
#
# Research question:
# Does satisfaction with one's personal financial situation
# predict confidence in government, and is this relationship
# moderated by compensation, benefits, and earnings stability?
#
# Secondary questions:
# 1. Does this relationship differ between Black and White
#    respondents?
# 2. Do objective job-quality dimensions moderate the
#    financial satisfaction -> confidence relationship
#    differently by race?
# 3. Do these relationships vary systematically over time?
#
# NOTE:
# confidence_government is coded:
#   1 = great deal of confidence
#   2 = only some confidence
#   3 = very little confidence
#
# Therefore, HIGHER values indicate LOWER confidence in
# government.
#
# Objective job-quality measures are assigned at the
# industry-year level. Conventional individual-level
# standard errors should therefore be interpreted cautiously.
# ============================================================


# ============================================================
# 0. Packages
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(broom)
library(car)



# ============================================================
# 1. Load data
# ============================================================

jqi_gss <- readRDS(
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "gss_job_quality_primary_2000_2024.rds"
  )
)


# ============================================================
# 2. Construct analysis variables
# ============================================================

jqi_confed_fin <- jqi_gss %>%
  mutate(
    
    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Financial satisfaction
    #
    # satfin:
    # 1 = pretty well satisfied
    # 2 = more or less satisfied
    # 3 = not satisfied at all
    #
    # Reverse so higher = greater satisfaction
    # --------------------------------------------------------
    
    financial_satisfaction = case_when(
      as.numeric(satfin) == 1 ~ 3,
      as.numeric(satfin) == 2 ~ 2,
      as.numeric(satfin) == 3 ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    
    
    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Confidence in government
    #
    # confed:
    # 1 = great deal
    # 2 = only some
    # 3 = very little
    #
    # Higher values = LOWER confidence
    # --------------------------------------------------------
    
    confidence_government = case_when(
      as.numeric(confed) %in% 1:3 ~ as.numeric(confed),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
    
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(financial_satisfaction),
    !is.na(confidence_government),
    !is.na(compensation),
    !is.na(benefits),
    !is.na(earnings_stability)
  )


# ============================================================
# 3. Inspect analytic sample
# ============================================================

nrow(jqi_confed_fin)

table(jqi_confed_fin$year)

summary(
  jqi_confed_fin %>%
    select(
      financial_satisfaction,
      confidence_government,
      compensation,
      benefits,
      earnings_stability
    )
)


# ============================================================
# 4. Basic relationship:
#    Financial satisfaction -> confidence in government
# ============================================================

m_confed_fin <- lm(
  confidence_government ~ financial_satisfaction,
  data = jqi_confed_fin
)

summary(m_confed_fin)


# ============================================================
# 5. Separate moderation models
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5a. Compensation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_confed_fin_comp <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    financial_satisfaction * compensation,
  data = jqi_confed_fin
)

summary(m_confed_fin_comp)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5b. Benefits
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_confed_fin_benefits <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    financial_satisfaction * benefits,
  data = jqi_confed_fin
)

summary(m_confed_fin_benefits)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5c. Earnings stability
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_confed_fin_earnings <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_confed_fin
)

summary(m_confed_fin_earnings)


# ============================================================
# 6. Joint JQI moderation model
# ============================================================

m_confed_fin_jqi <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    financial_satisfaction * compensation +
    financial_satisfaction * benefits +
    financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_confed_fin
)

summary(m_confed_fin_jqi)


# ============================================================
# 7. VIF diagnostics
# ============================================================

vif(m_confed_fin_jqi)


# ============================================================
# 8. Joint test of all financial-satisfaction × JQI
#    interactions
# ============================================================

linearHypothesis(
  m_confed_fin_jqi,
  c(
    "financial_satisfaction:compensation = 0",
    "financial_satisfaction:benefits = 0",
    "financial_satisfaction:earnings_stability = 0"
  )
)


# ============================================================
# 9. Race variable
# ============================================================

jqi_confed_fin_race <- jqi_confed_fin %>%
  mutate(
    race_group = case_when(
      racecen1 == 1 ~ "White",
      racecen1 == 2 ~ "Black",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    race_group = factor(
      race_group,
      levels = c("White", "Black")
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(race_group))


# ============================================================
# 10. Inspect racial sample
# ============================================================

table(jqi_confed_fin_race$race_group)

table(
  jqi_confed_fin_race$race_group,
  jqi_confed_fin_race$year
)


# ============================================================
# 11. Basic financial satisfaction × race model
# ============================================================

m_confed_fin_race <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    financial_satisfaction * race_group,
  data = jqi_confed_fin_race
)

summary(m_confed_fin_race)


# ============================================================
# 12. Separate race × JQI moderation models
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 12a. Compensation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_confed_fin_race_comp <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    financial_satisfaction * compensation +
    race_group * compensation +
    financial_satisfaction * race_group,
  data = jqi_confed_fin_race
)

summary(m_confed_fin_race_comp)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 12b. Benefits
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_confed_fin_race_benefits <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    financial_satisfaction * benefits +
    race_group * benefits +
    financial_satisfaction * race_group,
  data = jqi_confed_fin_race
)

summary(m_confed_fin_race_benefits)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 12c. Earnings stability
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_confed_fin_race_earnings <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability +
    race_group * earnings_stability +
    financial_satisfaction * race_group,
  data = jqi_confed_fin_race
)

summary(m_confed_fin_race_earnings)


# ============================================================
# 13. Full race × JQI model
# ============================================================

m_confed_fin_jqi_race <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    
    # Financial satisfaction × race
    financial_satisfaction * race_group +
    
    # Financial satisfaction × JQI
    financial_satisfaction * compensation +
    financial_satisfaction * benefits +
    financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability +
    
    # Race × JQI
    race_group * compensation +
    race_group * benefits +
    race_group * earnings_stability +
    
    # Three-way interactions:
    # Financial satisfaction × race × JQI
    financial_satisfaction * race_group * compensation +
    financial_satisfaction * race_group * benefits +
    financial_satisfaction * race_group * earnings_stability,
  
  data = jqi_confed_fin_race
)

summary(m_confed_fin_jqi_race)


# ============================================================
# 14. Test whether the financial satisfaction × race
#     relationship differs across JQI dimensions
# ============================================================

linearHypothesis(
  m_confed_fin_jqi_race,
  c(
    "financial_satisfaction:race_groupBlack:compensation = 0",
    "financial_satisfaction:race_groupBlack:benefits = 0",
    "financial_satisfaction:race_groupBlack:earnings_stability = 0"
  )
)


# ============================================================
# 15. Test race differences in the JQI main associations
# ============================================================

linearHypothesis(
  m_confed_fin_jqi_race,
  c(
    "race_groupBlack:compensation = 0",
    "race_groupBlack:benefits = 0",
    "race_groupBlack:earnings_stability = 0"
  )
)


# ============================================================
# 16. VIF diagnostics for race model
# ============================================================

vif(m_confed_fin_jqi_race)


# ============================================================
# 17. Implied financial-satisfaction slopes by race
# ============================================================

# Financial satisfaction slope by race in the basic model

race_fin_slopes <- tibble(
  race = c("White", "Black"),
  financial_satisfaction_slope = c(
    coef(m_confed_fin_race)["financial_satisfaction"],
    coef(m_confed_fin_race)["financial_satisfaction"] +
      coef(m_confed_fin_race)["financial_satisfaction:race_groupBlack"]
  )
)

print(race_fin_slopes)


# ============================================================
# 18. Implied JQI moderation slopes by race
# ============================================================

# Extract coefficients from the full model

coef_full_race <- coef(m_confed_fin_jqi_race)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Compensation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

comp_slopes <- tibble(
  race = c("White", "Black"),
  financial_satisfaction_x_compensation = c(
    coef_full_race["financial_satisfaction:compensation"],
    coef_full_race["financial_satisfaction:compensation"] +
      coef_full_race[
        "financial_satisfaction:race_groupBlack:compensation"
      ]
  )
)

print(comp_slopes)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Benefits
# ------------------------------------------------------------

benefits_slopes <- tibble(
  race = c("White", "Black"),
  financial_satisfaction_x_benefits = c(
    coef_full_race["financial_satisfaction:benefits"],
    coef_full_race["financial_satisfaction:benefits"] +
      coef_full_race[
        "financial_satisfaction:race_groupBlack:benefits"
      ]
  )
)

print(benefits_slopes)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Earnings stability
# ------------------------------------------------------------

earnings_slopes <- tibble(
  race = c("White", "Black"),
  financial_satisfaction_x_earnings_stability = c(
    coef_full_race["financial_satisfaction:earnings_stability"],
    coef_full_race[
      "financial_satisfaction:earnings_stability"
    ] +
      coef_full_race[
        "financial_satisfaction:race_groupBlack:earnings_stability"
      ]
  )
)

print(earnings_slopes)


# ============================================================
# 19. Temporal heterogeneity:
#     Do the three financial-satisfaction × JQI
#     relationships vary across years?
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Restricted model:
# common JQI moderation slopes across years
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_confed_fin_time_restricted <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    financial_satisfaction * compensation +
    financial_satisfaction * benefits +
    financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability +
    factor(year),
  data = jqi_confed_fin
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Full model:
# JQI moderation slopes allowed to vary by year
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_confed_fin_time_full <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    financial_satisfaction * compensation * factor(year) +
    financial_satisfaction * benefits * factor(year) +
    financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability * factor(year),
  data = jqi_confed_fin
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Omnibus temporal test
# ------------------------------------------------------------

anova(
  m_confed_fin_time_restricted,
  m_confed_fin_time_full
)


# ============================================================
# 20. Focused temporal test:
#     Does earnings stability moderate the relationship
#     differently across years?
# ============================================================

m_confed_fin_earnings_time_restricted <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    financial_satisfaction * compensation +
    financial_satisfaction * benefits +
    financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability +
    factor(year) +
    financial_satisfaction * compensation * factor(year) +
    financial_satisfaction * benefits * factor(year),
  data = jqi_confed_fin
)


m_confed_fin_earnings_time_full <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    financial_satisfaction * compensation +
    financial_satisfaction * benefits +
    financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability +
    factor(year) +
    financial_satisfaction * compensation * factor(year) +
    financial_satisfaction * benefits * factor(year) +
    financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability * factor(year),
  data = jqi_confed_fin
)


anova(
  m_confed_fin_earnings_time_restricted,
  m_confed_fin_earnings_time_full
)


# ============================================================
# 21. Optional focused temporal tests:
#     Compensation and benefits moderation
# ============================================================

m_confed_fin_comp_time_restricted <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    financial_satisfaction * compensation +
    financial_satisfaction * benefits +
    financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability +
    factor(year) +
    financial_satisfaction * benefits * factor(year) +
    financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability * factor(year),
  data = jqi_confed_fin
)

m_confed_fin_comp_time_full <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    financial_satisfaction * compensation * factor(year) +
    financial_satisfaction * benefits * factor(year) +
    financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability * factor(year),
  data = jqi_confed_fin
)

anova(
  m_confed_fin_comp_time_restricted,
  m_confed_fin_comp_time_full
)


m_confed_fin_benefits_time_restricted <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    financial_satisfaction * compensation +
    financial_satisfaction * benefits +
    financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability +
    factor(year) +
    financial_satisfaction * compensation * factor(year) +
    financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability * factor(year),
  data = jqi_confed_fin
)

m_confed_fin_benefits_time_full <- lm(
  confidence_government ~
    financial_satisfaction * compensation * factor(year) +
    financial_satisfaction * benefits * factor(year) +
    financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability * factor(year),
  data = jqi_confed_fin
)

anova(
  m_confed_fin_benefits_time_restricted,
  m_confed_fin_benefits_time_full
)


# ============================================================
# 22. Optional year-specific models
#     Useful if temporal heterogeneity is detected
# ============================================================

yearly_confed_fin <- jqi_confed_fin %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    
    model <- lm(
      confidence_government ~
        financial_satisfaction * compensation +
        financial_satisfaction * benefits +
        financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability,
      data = .x
    )
    
    broom::tidy(model)
    
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

print(yearly_confed_fin)


# ============================================================
# 23. Save model outputs in compact form
# ============================================================

# Main models

main_model_results <- bind_rows(
  
  broom::tidy(m_confed_fin) %>%
    mutate(model = "Baseline"),
  
  broom::tidy(m_confed_fin_comp) %>%
    mutate(model = "Financial satisfaction × Compensation"),
  
  broom::tidy(m_confed_fin_benefits) %>%
    mutate(model = "Financial satisfaction × Benefits"),
  
  broom::tidy(m_confed_fin_earnings) %>%
    mutate(model = "Financial satisfaction × Earnings stability"),
  
  broom::tidy(m_confed_fin_jqi) %>%
    mutate(model = "Joint JQI moderation")
  
) %>%
  select(model, everything())

print(main_model_results)


# ============================================================
# 24. Race model results
# ============================================================

race_model_results <- bind_rows(
  
  broom::tidy(m_confed_fin_race) %>%
    mutate(model = "Financial satisfaction × Race"),
  
  broom::tidy(m_confed_fin_race_comp) %>%
    mutate(model = "Race × Compensation"),
  
  broom::tidy(m_confed_fin_race_benefits) %>%
    mutate(model = "Race × Benefits"),
  
  broom::tidy(m_confed_fin_race_earnings) %>%
    mutate(model = "Race × Earnings stability"),
  
  broom::tidy(m_confed_fin_jqi_race) %>%
    mutate(model = "Full race × JQI model")
  
) %>%
  select(model, everything())

print(race_model_results)


# ============================================================
# Plot-only reversal of confidence in government
# ============================================================

# Do NOT alter the original confidence_government variable.
# Original coding:
#   1 = great deal of confidence
#   2 = only some
#   3 = very little
#
# Plot coding:
#   1 = very little confidence
#   2 = only some confidence
#   3 = great deal of confidence

jqi_confed_fin_race_plot <- jqi_confed_fin_race %>%
  mutate(
    confidence_government_plot = 4 - confidence_government
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Re-estimate the same full race × JQI model using the
# plot-oriented outcome
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_confed_fin_jqi_race_plot <- lm(
  confidence_government_plot ~
    financial_satisfaction * race_group +
    financial_satisfaction * compensation +
    financial_satisfaction * benefits +
    financial_satisfaction * earnings_stability +
    race_group * compensation +
    race_group * benefits +
    race_group * earnings_stability +
    financial_satisfaction * race_group * compensation +
    financial_satisfaction * race_group * benefits +
    financial_satisfaction * race_group * earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_confed_fin_race_plot
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Define meaningful levels of earnings stability
# ------------------------------------------------------------

earnings_mean <- mean(
  jqi_confed_fin_race_plot$earnings_stability,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

earnings_sd <- sd(
  jqi_confed_fin_race_plot$earnings_stability,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

earnings_levels <- c(
  "Low (-1 SD)" = earnings_mean - earnings_sd,
  "Mean" = earnings_mean,
  "High (+1 SD)" = earnings_mean + earnings_sd
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Create prediction grid
# ------------------------------------------------------------

prediction_grid <- expand_grid(
  financial_satisfaction = seq(
    min(
      jqi_confed_fin_race_plot$financial_satisfaction,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    max(
      jqi_confed_fin_race_plot$financial_satisfaction,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    length.out = 100
  ),
  
  earnings_level = names(earnings_levels),
  
  race_group = factor(
    c("White", "Black"),
    levels = levels(jqi_confed_fin_race_plot$race_group)
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    earnings_stability = unname(
      earnings_levels[earnings_level]
    ),
    
    compensation = mean(
      jqi_confed_fin_race_plot$compensation,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    benefits = mean(
      jqi_confed_fin_race_plot$benefits,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    earnings_level = factor(
      earnings_level,
      levels = c(
        "Low (-1 SD)",
        "Mean",
        "High (+1 SD)"
      )
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate predictions and 95% confidence intervals
# ------------------------------------------------------------

prediction_results <- predict(
  m_confed_fin_jqi_race_plot,
  newdata = prediction_grid,
  interval = "confidence",
  level = 0.95
)

prediction_grid <- prediction_grid %>%
  mutate(
    predicted_confidence = prediction_results[, "fit"],
    conf_low = prediction_results[, "lwr"],
    conf_high = prediction_results[, "upr"]
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_fin_earnings_race <- ggplot(
  prediction_grid,
  aes(
    x = financial_satisfaction,
    y = predicted_confidence,
    color = race_group,
    fill = race_group,
    linetype = race_group,
    group = interaction(race_group, earnings_level)
  )
) +
  
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = conf_low,
      ymax = conf_high
    ),
    alpha = 0.15,
    color = NA
  ) +
  
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  
  facet_wrap(
    ~ earnings_level,
    nrow = 1
  ) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "White" = "darkgreen",
      "Black" = "blue"
    )
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "White" = "darkgreen",
      "Black" = "blue"
    )
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Financial Satisfaction and Confidence in Government",
    subtitle = "Moderated by earnings stability",
    x = "Financial satisfaction",
    y = "Predicted confidence in government",
    color = "Race",
    fill = "Race",
    linetype = "Race",
    caption = paste(
      "Shaded areas represent 95% confidence intervals.",
      "Earnings stability is evaluated at −1 SD, the mean, and +1 SD.",
      "Compensation and benefits are held at their sample means."
    )
  ) +
  
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = 1:3,
    labels = c(
      "Very little",
      "Some",
      "Great deal"
    )
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray30"),
    plot.caption = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      color = "gray40"
    ),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Display
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_fin_earnings_race


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Save
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  here(
    "04_figures",
    "Financial_Satisfaction_Earnings_Stability_Race_Confidence_Government_CI.png"
  ),
  p_fin_earnings_race,
  width = 10,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Save
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  here(
    "04_figures",
    "Financial_Satisfaction_Earnings_Stability_Race_Confidence_Government_CI.png"
  ),
  p_fin_earnings_race,
  width = 10,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)


# ============================================================
# 25. Save results
# ============================================================

write_csv(
  main_model_results,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "JQI_FinancialSatisfaction_ConfidenceGovernment_MainModels.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  race_model_results,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "JQI_FinancialSatisfaction_ConfidenceGovernment_RaceModels.csv"
  )

write_csv(
  yearly_confed_fin,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "JQI_FinancialSatisfaction_ConfidenceGovernment_YearModels.csv"
  )
)


# ============================================================
# 26. Session information
# ============================================================

sessionInfo()
```
